ppi_focus: OBD scan: ECU calibration ID vs stock, readiness monitors, stored/pending codes; confirm no tune and smog eligibility.
Engine bay: intake, headers or over-pipe, aftermarket parts without CARB EO stickers.
Clutch engagement point, slip under load in 4th–5th, throwout bearing noise, gearbox synchro grind on fast shifts.
Underside: scrapes from lowering, front lip/subframe damage, any coilover or arm changes, diff and transmission leaks.
Paint meter on all panels, especially front end and rear quarters, since aero installs can hide repairs.
Rear wing and trunk mounting: drilled holes, water ingress into the trunk, and the loose trunk-lid wiring.
Tire DOT dates and wear pattern (inner-edge wear suggests aggressive alignment or track use).
Oil condition and level, and any signs of oil consumption; compression/leakdown if any track use is admitted.
Brake pad/rotor condition and brake fluid moisture test.
what_would_change_verdict: Up: the Carfax shows one owner, no accidents and regular dealer service, plus a clean ECU calibration and stock powertrain at PPI.
Up: price negotiated to the $18,999 sticker or below, with documented brake fluid and coolant service.
Down: evidence of a tune, headers, track use or lowering damage, or the Carfax shows an accident or more owners.
Down: the trunk-lid wiring or wing mounting reveals water leaks or a poor-quality install.
evidence.mission_note: A nearby, inspectable, reliable manual within budget, so it could only serve as a pragmatic bridge. However, the buyer context says the BRZ/86 stays out, and red with aftermarket aero is far from his preferred spec.
evidence.rationale: The listing establishes a manual first-generation BRZ in red with black interior, claimed at 51,610 miles, one owner and a clean title, with a Carfax offered only as a short link that was not examined here. Photos show the car on a Toyota dealer lot despite the private-seller name, and a windshield price of $18,999 against the $19,999 ask. Visible aftermarket carbon-look rear wing, diffuser, lip and side skirts, plus loose wiring inside the trunk lid, indicate an enthusiast-modified car. That puts the profile's track-use and tune questions squarely in play, and the listing answers neither. No VIN, service records, tire dates or engine-bay photos are provided, so documentation and mechanical condition rest on seller prose. The asking price sits at the top of the fair-value range with no records or stock originality to support it. Logistics are excellent at roughly 20 miles away on a dealer lot. The model is one the buyer context says stays out of the search.
evidence.next_action: Message the seller for the VIN, the full Carfax PDF and an out-the-door price, and ask directly about tune and track history before arranging any inspection.
